blocks.en: Abstract
blocks.zh: 摘要

blocks.en: Vision-Language-Action (VLA) models enable end-to-end robot control, but inference is increasingly expensive. Each decision processes hundreds of visual tokens, often across multiple cameras, leading to substantial computation while allowing irrelevant background content to distract action prediction under distribution shift. We argue that these issues stem from two complementary forms of redundancy: many visual tokens are spatially irrelevant, while attention over the remaining tokens is often misallocated. Based on this observation, we propose T3R, a Training-Free Two-Stage Token Refinement framework. In the first stage, segmentation-guided token pruning removes irrelevant visual patches to reduce computation and eliminate distracting context. In the second stage, saliency-guided attention biasing reallocates attention toward action-critical visual regions and language instructions within the retained tokens. Together, pruning produces a cleaner candidate set, while attention biasing further emphasizes the most decision-relevant evidence, yielding a better accuracy-efficiency frontier than either stage alone. On LIBERO-Spatial, T3R removes 85% of scene-camera visual tokens while essentially matching the unpruned success rate, and improves success by up to 7 percentage points under out-of-distribution object-placement perturbations. The timing comparison attributes 7.8 ms per inference call to pruning and attention-bias application. As input resolution increases, LLM-forward profiling shows up to a 3.3x speedup over the unpruned baseline. Evaluations across LIBERO, SIMPLER, and RoboTwin with three VLA backbones show the strongest accuracy-efficiency benefits in multi-camera settings. These results demonstrate that training-free token refinement is a practical approach to efficient and robust VLA inference.
blocks.zh: 视觉-语言-动作(VLA)模型可以实现端对端机器人控制,但推论越来越昂贵. 每个决定都会处理数百个视觉符号,常常跨越多个相机,导致大量计算,同时允许不相关的背景内容分散分布转移下的行动预测. 我们认为,这些问题来自两种互补的冗余形式:许多视觉标志在空间上无关紧要,而对其他标志的注意往往被错分配。 基于这一看法,我们提议采用T3R,即免费培训双层托肯改进框架。 在第一阶段,分块制导的令牌浏览会移除无关的视觉补丁以减少计算,并消除分散上下文. 在第二阶段,引人注意的显著偏重是将注意力重新分配给保留标志内的动作关键视觉区域和语言指示。 抽查共同产生一套较清洁的候选人,而注意力偏差则进一步强调与决策最相关的证据,从而产生比两个阶段都更好的准确效率前沿。 在LIBERO-Spatrial上,T3R移除85%的场景-相机视觉标志,同时基本匹配未刷成功率,并在分配外物体放置扰动下提升成功率高达7个百分点. 计时比较将每个推论的7.8 ms 表示为 prun 和 ocredit-bias 应用. 随着输入分辨率的提高,LLM前向剖面显示比未铺设基线加快3.3x。 在LIBERO、SIMPLER和RoboTwin三个VLA主干网进行的评价显示,在多镜头环境中,精确效率效益最大。 这些结果表明,完善无培训标志性的工作是有效和有力地推论志愿军的一种实用方法。

blocks.en:
Vision-Language-Action (VLA) models ( Brohan et al., 2023a ; Black et al., 2024 ; Kim et al., 2024 ) provide a unified
interface from pixels and language to robot actions, but this generality carries
a substantial inference burden. At every decision step, the model propagates a
long visual sequence through a large language backbone. In a typical
OpenVLA-style setup, a 224 × 224 224\times 224 image produces 256 256 visual

any action token is predicted. Attending over such long sequences at every
control step is expensive and increases latency, which is detrimental to
real-time control and can further induce observation–action distribution shift
through stale observations and delayed actuation ( Arachchige et al., 2025 ) .

Many visual tokens are weakly coupled to the language
instruction ( Chen et al., 2024 ; Shang et al., 2024 ) . These tokens can diffuse attention and distract
action prediction, especially under viewpoint or object-placement shifts.
Effective refinement must both remove irrelevant tokens and reinforce
instruction-relevant evidence among those retained.

blocks.en:
Building on this view, we introduce T3R, a training-free two-stage token
refinement framework. Stage 1 performs segmentation-guided token pruning with
position preservation, so compression happens before the VLA decoder and
every transformer layer benefits from a shorter input. Stage 2 compensates for
pruning-induced information loss by injecting task relevance into the retained
sequence: saliency-guided attention biasing in intermediate layers steers
action-token queries toward instruction-salient words and retained task-relevant
regions.

blocks.zh: 2. 相关工作

blocks.en:
Vision-Language-Action models. VLA methods cast robot control as conditional sequence modeling over
observations, instructions, and actions. RT-1/RT-2 ( Brohan et al., 2023b ; Brohan et al., 2023a ) established
large-scale vision-language pretraining for manipulation, while OpenVLA and
OpenVLA-OFT ( Kim et al., 2024 ; Kim et al., 2025 ) improved openness and adaptation
efficiency. Parallel efforts including π 0 \pi_{0} / π 0.5 \pi_{0.5} ( Black et al., 2024 ; Physical Intelligence et al., 2025 ) ,
CogACT ( Li et al., 2024b ) , and GR00T ( NVIDIA et al., 2025 ) scale model capacity and control
fidelity. Inference still relies on propagating long visual token sequences
through heavy backbones, leaving efficiency and robustness under perturbation as
open bottlenecks.

blocks.en:
Token-efficient inference. Token reduction has been studied in vision transformers and multimodal LLMs via
pruning, merging, and routing ( Bolya et al., 2023 ; Rao et al., 2021 ; Chen et al., 2024 ; Shang et al., 2024 ) . In embodied
settings, EfficientVLA, LightVLA, and TeamVLA ( Yang et al., 2025 ; Jiang et al., 2025 ; Ye et al., 2025 ) adapt these ideas with task-aware scoring and runtime compression; FastV ( Chen et al., 2024 ) prunes visual tokens after an early decoder layer; ADP ( Pei et al., 2025 ) performs
action-aware dynamic pruning; and VLA-Cache ( Xu et al., 2025 ) reuses KV-cache
entries across frames. T3R targets the harder decoder-entry regime:
tokens are removed before any decoder layer, benefiting all layers, but
selection is irreversible and lacks internal attention guidance. T3R
addresses this by coupling external vision-language grounding with post-pruning
attention repair. T3R and VLA-Cache are complementary (spatial vs. temporal redundancy).

Resolution scaling and hardware implications. The effective per-token marginal cost rises from 0.040 0.040 ms at sequence length ∼ \sim 200 to 0.064 0.064 ms at ∼ \sim 500, marking the transition from a

stays in the cheaper bandwidth-bound regime as resolution grows, while the
unpruned baseline enters the quadratic compute-bound regime.
LLM-forward profiling shows up to a 3.3 × 3.3\times speedup at 768 px.
For accelerator co-design the implication is concrete: pre-decoder pruning shifts
the operating point back toward the memory-bound regime that current LLM
inference hardware handles most efficiently. Using the measured LLM cost on an
L40S and adding a fixed 48.6 ms non-LLM cost, we project end-to-end inference
latencies of 100 / 115 / 132 100/115/132 ms at 384 / 512 / 768 384/512/768 px for T3R,
versus the baseline’s 144 / 182 / 327 144/182/327 ms and ADP’s 109 / 145 / 238 109/145/238 ms, a 2.47 × 2.47\times projected speedup over baseline at 768 px, versus ADP’s 1.37 × 1.37\times . These projections do not independently measure refinement

blocks.en: 4.8. Failure Analysis and Limitations
blocks.zh: 4.8. 失败分析和限制

blocks.en:
T3R underperforms TeamVLA on LIBERO-Object (82% vs. 86%). These tasks
place a source object into a visually dominant destination (e.g., a basket), so
SigLIP similarity splits between the two and EfficientTAM segments the wrong
region or produces an overly narrow mask. Multi-phase LIBERO-Long tasks (e.g., “put the
bowl in the drawer and close it”) pose a related issue: the relevant region
shifts mid-episode, but similarity is computed from the full instruction and does
not adapt to the current phase, so pruning may mask regions that become critical
later. More broadly, (i) Stage 1 depends on promptable segmentation as an
intermediate prior and inherits its failure modes on merged or coarse
boundaries; (ii) IG adds a one-time per-task cost that may not amortize over short
task runs or meet strict initialization deadlines; and (iii) our single-camera zero-shot results
(Sec. 4.5 ) show the method offers little benefit when the sensor
suite carries little redundancy. Phase-aware re-prompting and camera-adaptive
budgets are natural extensions.

blocks.en: 5. Conclusion
blocks.zh: 5 (韩语). 结论

blocks.en:
We presented T3R, a training-free two-stage framework that couples
segmentation-guided token pruning with saliency-guided
attention biasing. On LIBERO-Spatial with OpenVLA-OFT, it removes 85% of
scene-camera visual tokens while retaining success within 1 pp of baseline,
reduces VLA inference latency, and improves OOD robustness by up to 7 pp.
Evaluations on CogACT and π 0.5 \pi_{0.5} across SIMPLER and RoboTwin suggest that
overlapping multi-camera evidence provides more headroom for token pruning.
From a design perspective, the value of T3R lies in where it
acts. By discarding irrelevant tokens before decoder entry, every transformer
layer operates on the shorter sequence, so the retained tokens stay in the
cheaper bandwidth-bound regime even as resolution grows, yielding a
projected speedup of up to 2.47 × 2.47\times at 768 768 px. Mask updates run asynchronously, while IG computation
is amortized across each task’s episodes. Because the pipeline is training-free and leaves the
underlying VLA weights unchanged, it applies directly to existing pretrained
policies. Together, these properties make
task-conditioned, pre-decoder sparsification a practical, first-class knob for
co-designing efficient embodied inference systems. Across scenes, its adaptive
budget retains 9–15 patches in sparse cases and up to 121 in clutter, while
middle-layer biasing recovers 6 pp of the prune-only accuracy loss. Together
with the 93.9% attention-sparsity result, these measurements explain why
aggressive pruning remains viable and when additional evidence must be retained.
